findings.reason: with no declared edge a coordinator can dispatch §37 against §9's absent `session=` argument, and the worker is fenced out of `resumption.py` to add it, so the node blocks or invents the interface §9 owns.
findings.text: §37 states "Build it after §9 has landed" and its deliverable calls `sweep` with the session §9 adds to `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 24) records no `s37:[s9]` edge, and §37's write paths (`reckon/crew/runs.py`, its test) do not overlap §9's (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, its test), so the dispatcher's scope-conflict check cannot refuse an out-of-order or parallel dispatch — the guard the earlier §33/§34 declination relied on is absent here

findings.reason: the citation is the plan's evidence for "the reflex already scopes itself", and a pointer to a non-existent test is worse than none; correcting it is a one-line edit to the sentence the node's premise rests on.
findings.text: §9 cites `tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py::test_the_sweep_bookends_only_its_sessions_runs` as the test that holds the reflex's self-scoping, but the test is named `test_the_sweep_bookends_only_its_own_sessions_runs` (word "own" omitted), so a reader following the anchor to confirm the claim greps and finds nothing

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §9's citation of the reflex's confirming test names a test that does not exist under that name; every other anchor checked resolves (`_sweep_lapsed_holds` and `sweep(project, dry_run=dry_run)` in `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:93,103`, `sweep` and its two passes in `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1651,1888`, `_sweeping_session` in `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1000`, `dispatch_awaiting_reviews(session=...)` in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:360`, `watch` in `reckon/crew/runs.py:3081`, and both extensionless measurement-plan links resolving to `the-monitor-under-measurement.html#s4` and `#s7`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §9 and §37 each name measurable cases and a declared negative control (both logged under the run directory), and §9's two controls can each fail (resume pass unscoped resumes both; reflex pass called without `session=` from an unregistered process reviews both, since `_sweeping_session` returns empty for a process holding no registration).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both nodes write their tests under `tests/` and log their controls under the crew run directory, neither a session scratchpad nor a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed units introduce no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers; §9 and §37 name only existing mechanism symbols (`sweep`, `dispatch_awaiting_reviews`, `_sweeping_session`, `_sweep_lapsed_holds`) and propose no new plan-labelled symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §9's root cause (the resume pass takes every lapsed run from `list_live` whatever its session; the reflex has self-scoped since `5b98a1c2f`) matches the code at `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1694,1888` and `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:103`, its mechanism (an explicit session passed to both passes) produces §9's done-when, and its caller is named (`_sweep_lapsed_holds`); §37's mechanism runs on the named caller's tick (`watch` in `reckon/crew/runs.py`) and its explicit session is exactly what §9 will add to `sweep`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 is one change (an explicit session on both sweep passes) and §37 is one change (the watcher sweeps unfollowed sessions).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §37's deliverable calls `sweep` with the session "§9 makes possible", but `plan-section-depends-on` (line 24) carries no `s37:[s9]` edge and the two sections share no write path, so nothing enforces the order §37 requires.
